Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Review of Arroyo Precision Works — 5 stars

Arroyo Precision Works built the camera-to-dewar adapter plate and light baffle tube for our near-IR camera, and I want to write this up properly rather than just say "great shop." I've read a lot of vendor reviews while trying to find someone who could do this work, and if you're an instrument-mechanical shop or a lab that has been burned by a big vendor, I think the details here are worth your time.

The job was a 6061-T6 adapter plate and a 6061-T6 light baffle tube with internal threads, both black anodized, for a near-infrared camera we're taking down to Palomar on November 18. Another shop quoted us six weeks. Arroyo quoted 21 days on the PO and the parts were on our bench nine days after the PO was issued. Nine days, not twenty-one. I still don't know how they managed that with the team they have, but that's the difference I care about when a run date is fixed on a telescope.

Our fit test on November 9 was clean. All eight screws went into the plate on the first try, no forcing, no relaunching of the hole pattern. Flatness across the face came in under 0.01 mm on a dial indicator, which is the number that decides whether I sleep before a observing run. The baffle threads were smooth and clean, and the dark test showed no light leak at all (lab lights on, 300 s dark frame, compared against a closed dewar). The anodize came back even with no bare spots and no drips around the bore.

One more thing, because it says more about how they work than anything else: I sent a drawing with the bolt circle in the wrong units — 4.125 instead of 104.8 mm — because I copied it from an old drawing for our previous camera. That mistake was entirely mine, not theirs. Ruben wrote back before they cut anything and asked me to confirm; Tiff flagged it at the machine. Had they just cut the plate, the screws would have landed inside the bore and we would have found out about it the week of a telescope run. They caught a customer error that was in no way their fault, and they handled it the way you'd want a shop to handle it: asked, waited for my answer, then confirmed before touching metal.

Ruben also dropped the parts off at Robinson Lab himself on his way to a supplier in Glendale, and didn't charge for the delivery. Small thing, but it saved us a trip and a day of schedule.

For our near-IR camera I won't be going anywhere else, and I'd say the same to anyone else building optics or instrument mechanicals: Arroyo reads the drawings, quotes honestly, and delivers early instead of late. If your lab is tired of six-week lead times, give them a try.

5 stars. I'm also hoping our purchasing office puts them on the preferred vendor list for next fiscal year — and I'd encourage other requesters to say the same when they're eligible.

— Lin Wei, Astronomy, Pasadena

Subject: Arroyo review draft — flatness good, we're clear for the 18th

Marta, yes — flatness was under 0.01 mm across the face on the dial indicator, all eight screws in with no forcing, and the dark test showed no light leak with the baffle installed. Anodize is even with no bare spots. We're good for the Palomar run on the 18th, and nothing in the hardware is holding up an instrument change request.

I've written the Arroyo review and have it in draft on the CampusSource page so I can read it over before I post it. I kept it to what I can actually vouch for: the nine-day delivery against a 21-day quote, the six-week quote I got elsewhere, the fit test numbers, and the bolt circle story — I own that one, the drawing error was mine, and Ruben caught it before they cut. I also said explicitly that I'd like to see them added to the preferred vendor list.

Purchasing, this is the kind of feedback you're asking requesters to leave for non-preferred vendors. Arroyo came in well under their quoted lead time, caught a drawing error before it cost anyone money, and delivered to Robinson at no charge. They read that page when other labs and your colleagues are deciding, so I hope it helps the case for adding them next fiscal year. Let me know if you want anything changed before I post.
